bull.b: The shift to strong profitability and margins improves internal funding capacity and reduces reliance on external capital. However, durability depends on recurring product sales because recent results also benefited from a milestone and an R&D law credit.

A cash-rich, debt-free balance sheet gives Protalix flexibility to fund manufacturing, clinical development and regulatory work without near-term financing pressure. This strengthens resilience while the company advances its pipeline and commercial programs.

Additional geographic access and less frequent dosing can broaden Elfabrio adoption and improve its competitive positioning in Fabry disease. Partner-led commercialization also allows Protalix to participate in growth without building a large direct sales infrastructure.

bear.b: Dependence on Chiesi and uneven ordering can make revenue timing difficult to forecast, even when underlying demand is healthy. This concentration also gives partner decisions greater influence over manufacturing volumes, cash conversion and reported results.

The milestone materially inflated first-half revenue and makes year-over-year performance less representative of recurring commercial economics. Future results will need sustained Elfabrio sales and supply revenue to maintain the improved earnings profile.

Immunogenicity and infusion-related reaction concerns may constrain dose selection, complicate development and delay advancement of PRX-115. Uncertainty over the final regimen could affect clinical timelines, development costs and the program’s eventual market positioning.
